mechanism: Why 4 cores give only 1.63x on quad_n9: (a) about 10 % of the counted reduction ran on one thread. That is 40.9 M of 399.4 M row ops: the B' in-block finish (26.0 M), B' blocks too narrow to pass the gate (2.5 M), the deferred RREF store (9.4 M) and small pair blocks (2.3 M). Amdahl then caps the reduction at 3.1x. (b) The AVX-512 update kernel is memory-bound (scalar is only 1.4x slower), so the parallel part scales about 1.8x. (c) Phases outside the count do not scale: final interreduction (~21 ms), basis update (~8 ms), matrix build (~11-13 ms). Symbolic preprocessing ran round-parallel with 3-4 rayon dispatches per round and was slower in parallel than serial (31.8 vs 22.8 ms). Why FL and threads hurt cubic_n5: n_free is below 512, so every 64-reducer B' block failed the width gate (64*n_free > PAR_WORK). FL therefore ran 97.9 % on one thread, while with FL off the cascade ran in parallel; parallel symbolic added dispatch overhead on top. Fixes, all default and all restored by F4_FP_PAR_OLD=1: (1) B' built in column tiles (bprime_tiled). Each free column of B' depends only on the same column of earlier rows, so tiles with equal work are independent and need no serial finish. Tiles are used only with more than 1 thread and up to 2^26 entries; otherwise row blocks are used, gated on update work rather than width, and the in-block finish is tiled. F4_FP_PAR_FL_MODE=tiles|rows forces either. (2) The pair-row block gate now uses entries*n_free, with block size adapted to the thread count. (3) Symbolic preprocessing is round-parallel only from 1024 seed rows; rounds with fewer than 256 frontier rows run serially; the reducer search is gated on the amount of work. (4) F4_FP_PAR_PROF=1 prints per-section counts of row ops run serially vs spread.
prediction: Written before measuring: fingerprints identical at 1, 2 and 4 threads. field_ops within +-1 %. quad_n9 one-thread row-op share below 5 %. quad_n9 at 4 threads ~150-180 -> 120-140 ms. cubic_n5 ~18 -> 14-15 ms, no longer slower than FL off or 1 thread. Overall 4-thread speed-up on quad_n9 capped near 2x by the serial phases outside the count.
toggle: F4_FP_PAR_OLD=1 (restores the old thread dispatch exactly; also F4_FP_PAR_FL_MODE=tiles|rows, F4_FP_PAR_SYM_SEEDS, F4_FP_PAR_SYM_FRONTIER, F4_FP_PAR_FL_WORK, F4_FP_PAR_FL_INBLOCK, F4_FP_PAR_FL_TILES knobs; F4_FP_PAR_PROF=1 diagnostics)
correctness: Final build 4 (bin4, sha256 ebbb50aa...): f4_fp_bench "3 large" was run in 9 arms: new default, F4_FP_PAR_OLD=1 and F4_FP_PAR_FL_MODE=tiles, each at RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1, 2 and 4. All 9 match the baseline binary exactly on all 13 cases, in basis_fp, solve_fp, field_ops, solve_field_ops, steps, max_rows, max_cols, basis_len and solutions. Examples: quad_n9 5a5d7dea3744f69d with 399,396,830 field_ops; quad_n8 539b2a77ccede549 with 56,664,766; cubic_n5 fbab6676a859b968 with 12,712,111; overdet_n12 3333741564c1aa21 with 84,352,865. Build 3 had passed the same check (baseline, new and old at 1, 2 and 4 threads). No counter changed. cargo test --release --lib f4_fp: 96 passed, including the new bprime_tiled_matches_row_build and finish_block_tiled tests. Not checked: GF(2) and crossbred, which are out of scope because this file does not touch them.
deterministic_evidence: The one-thread row-op share comes from F4_FP_PAR_PROF=1 over the first f4 call (steps plus interreduction). Results, old vs new: quad_n9 40,931,644 (10.2 %) -> 10,169,782 (2.5 %); quad_n8 41.4 % -> 5.6 %; cubic_n5 97.9 % -> 12.4 %; overdet_n12 6.2 % -> 5.3 %. The new shares are the same at 2 and 4 threads. The counted Amdahl bound for the quad_n9 reduction at 4 threads rises from 3.1x to 3.7x. 9,446,366 of the remaining 10.17 M one-thread ops on quad_n9 are the deferred-RREF sequential store, which this patch leaves unchanged.
indicative_timing: Indicative only: shared VM at load 2-3, 7 interleaved rounds (t8.jsonl, build 4). Times are base -> new in ms. At 4 threads: quad_n7 13.7->9.9 (1.39x), quad_n8 45.9->39.8 (1.15x), quad_n9 166.2->147.2 (1.13x), cubic_n5 17.5->15.4 (1.13x), overdet_n10 27.2->23.5 (1.16x), overdet_n12 45.5->42.4 (1.07x). At 1 thread the change is neutral (0.91-1.08); overdet_n10 at 0.91 was 0.97-1.07 in other runs. 4-thread vs 1-thread scaling on quad_n9: base 1.34x -> new 1.48x here, 1.25x -> 1.52x in an earlier calmer run (t4.jsonl, build 3: quad_n9 151.4->127.0). cubic_n5 at 4 threads is no longer slower than at 1 thread (15.4 vs 15.4; baseline 17.5 vs 15.8). Build 3 had a 1-thread cost on cubic_n5 and quad_n7 (0.91-0.93) from tile overhead; build 4 fixes it by using row blocks on one thread. The prediction for quad_n9 (120-140 ms) was not fully met.
risks: The cutoffs (SYM_SEEDS 1024, SYM_FRONTIER 256, FL_WORK 2^17, FL_INBLOCK 2^16, FL_TILES_MAX_ENTRIES 2^26) were tuned on this 4-core VM and 6 cases only. Tiled B' holds a second copy of B' (bounded at 256 MB). quad_n10/n11 were not timed; round-parallel symbolic stays on at 1024 or more seeds, which preserves the win the msolve parity report measured on quad_n11. The patch is large (about 1168 diff lines, mostly additive new functions and profiling counters) and touches reduce_pairs_fl, reduce_pairs_blocked and symbolic dispatch, so it may conflict with other leads' edits to f4_fp.rs. The remaining serial work is the deferred store, interreduction symbolic and basis update. All results [pcc:unverified]; wall-clock needs the serial A/A stage.
